article.title: Judge Approves $7.25bn Bayer Settlement Over Roundup Cancer Claims
article.summary: A Missouri state court judge has approved Bayer's $7.25bn settlement to resolve approximately 65,000 lawsuits alleging that its glyphosate-based weedkiller, Roundup, causes cancer, bringing a close to nearly a decade of heavy litigation for the German company.

article.content_html:
Missouri Judge Approves Massive Bayer Payout

A Missouri state court judge in St. Louis has officially approved Bayer’s $7.25bn settlement of lawsuits alleging that its flagship weedkiller, Roundup, causes cancer. Judge Timothy Boyer ruled that the settlement agreement is "fair, reasonable and adequate," successfully overruling objections that individual payouts to cancer victims would be too low compared to previous settlements. The judge emphasized that delaying payouts further could force terminally ill victims to wait an indeterminate number of years before receiving compensation.

The monumental settlement, originally announced in February, was designed to resolve nearly all current and future Roundup claims across the United States. Bayer’s CEO, Bill Anderson, described the court's final approval as a decisive milestone in the company's overarching strategy to mitigate the operational and financial risks associated with pending and future litigation.

Key Facts and Court Decisions

  • Judge Timothy Boyer approved the $7.25bn settlement in St. Louis, dismissing objections regarding individual payout amounts.
  • The agreement addresses approximately 65,000 claims filed in US state and federal courts from individuals who developed cancer after using Roundup.
  • The ruling arrives just five months after the US Supreme Court overturned a separate $1.25m jury award in a pivotal decision favoring Bayer.

Decade of Legal Challenges for Bayer

Bayer has faced extensive legal turmoil over Roundup since it acquired Monsanto—the original producer of the weedkiller—for $63bn in 2018. The ensuing litigation has severely impacted the German company, causing its share price to plummet by 46% over the period. Although Bayer previously settled a large portion of the Roundup litigation for $10.9bn in 2020, it struggled to secure court approval for future claims until now.

Throughout the legal battle, Bayer has consistently maintained that Roundup and its active ingredient, glyphosate, are safe, citing decades of scientific studies. The latest legal landscape also shifted following a 7-2 US Supreme Court decision ruling that federal pesticide laws bar state-law failure-to-warn claims. Christopher Seeger, an attorney representing numerous plaintiffs, noted that while this supreme court decision narrowed victims' options, the current settlement moves forward to provide financial relief as quickly as possible.
